ledger.sentence: The WHO's Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE) met from 5 to 8 October 2026.
SAGE recommends HPV vaccination of girls aged 9 to 14 years with a single-dose schedule, which it describes as the most efficient immunization strategy for cervical cancer prevention.

ledger.sentence: SAGE says countries may consider routine single-dose vaccination of girls aged 4 to 8 years.

A message from the director of the World Health Organization's immunization department, dated 29 October 2026, reports on the October meeting of its Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), held from 5 to 8 October.

SAGE recommends human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination of girls aged 9 to 14 years using a single-dose schedule, which it describes as the most efficient immunization strategy for cervical cancer prevention.
ledger.note: Search 34. [second pass: edited to unsupported correction: Single dose for girls 9-14 is stated by the highlights and the director message. The wording "goals of the global cervical cancer strategy" was not se]

ledger.sentence: According to the meeting highlights, countries may also consider routine single-dose vaccination of girls aged 4 to 8 years, and single-dose coverage could later extend to further target groups.
The director's message adds that a single dose can be used for people up to age 30.
The 2022 SAGE position allowed one or two doses for the primary target group of girls aged 9 to 14; the October 2026 advice is for a single dose.
